title: Ready screen with one big Start
what: Nose 4 and mouth 6 icons at the top, the technique name Calm, one sentence on what it does, a large glowing round Start button flanked by vibration and settings buttons, and a 5 min picker pill below.
takeaway: One huge Start target with the duration as a small pill underneath means the default session starts in one tap, and the length is still changeable.

title: Ready screen with length and breath type
what: A preview circle reading Inhale, Nose above LENGTH tiles for 1, 3, 5 and 10 min, a BREATH TYPE toggle of Normal or Easier, and a Start button showing the 10 energy reward.
takeaway: An Easier option is a kind way to serve older users who cannot hold long breaths, and showing the reward on Start tells people what finishing earns.

title: Ready screen with technique, duration and sound tiles
what: A box outline, the name Box Breath with a BALANCE tag and arrows to swap technique, a short description, three tiles for Technique, Duration 2 min and Sound Segue, and a round play button.
takeaway: Three summary tiles show every setting at once without opening them, so the user can check and go.

title: Paused with Resume and End Early
what: The breathing shape is faded to grey outlines, a thin top progress bar reads 00:54 left, and two controls sit at the bottom: a black Resume pill and a plain End Early text link.
takeaway: Pause greys the shape so the state is obvious, and the primary action is Resume while ending is a quieter secondary link.

title: Running player with scrubber and skip 10
what: Title 4:8, Breathwork, 5 min top left with an X top right, a soft gradient background, a thin progress bar with 4:14 remaining, and skip back 10, pause and skip forward 10 controls.
takeaway: An audio style player suits guided voice sessions, though skip buttons add clutter a simple breathing timer does not need.

title: Paused timer with word Paused beside play
what: Focus with a 3:10 PM to 3:55 PM range, a hourglass inside a ring, a big 44:50 time and the word Paused next to a black play pill.
takeaway: Writing Paused in plain text next to the play button removes any doubt about whether the session is still running.

title: End session early confirm that keeps data
what: An In Session screen with an End early outline button, and a system alert titled End session early? with the line Your session details will be saved, and Cancel or OK.
takeaway: Ending early asks once and promises the partial session is saved, so no effort is lost and nobody feels punished.

title: End this workout full screen confirm
what: A full screen asking End this workout? with This workout will be saved to your workout history, a summary row 60 min Full Body Strength 7/7 blocks 3:12, and END and RESUME buttons.
takeaway: Showing what has been done so far in the confirm helps the user decide, and Resume sits right under End as an equal size escape.

title: Good job with No, A little, Yes
what: Good job! and You've Completed Meditation above a 01:00 TIME chip, Add note, share and star at the top, and a bottom panel asking Did you enjoy this Meditation? with No, A little and Yes tiles drawn as empty, half and full circles, plus Skip & Finish.
takeaway: Three filled circle tiles are a readable, language light rating, and Skip & Finish keeps the rating optional.

title: Good Work with feeling compared to before
what: A gold badge with a tick, the title Good Work!, the question How are you feeling now? and three stacked options Better than before, About the same and Worse than before, with a Continue button.
takeaway: Asking compared to before is easier to answer than a mood scale and gives a direct before and after signal for breathing.

title: How'd it go reflection
what: An orange illustration header, How'd it go? and Take a moment to reflect, with four full width answers: Great, I'm feeling relaxed; Challenging, but I'm eager to keep trying; Difficult, I'm feeling discouraged; I'm not sure.
takeaway: Full sentence answers let a user say it was hard without choosing a low number, and include an honest not sure option.

title: Today list as a vertical timeline
what: Good Evening, Alex and Start your day over three cards joined by a dashed line on the left: the first has a green tick, the second an orange filled dot as the current item, and the third an empty circle. Each card shows type and minutes.
takeaway: A rail of tick, current dot and empty circle shows done, next and later at a glance without striking anything through or moving cards.

title: To-do with 3 of 4 completed and strike through
what: A week strip with today ticked, a To-do header with 3 of 4 completed on the right, three rows struck through with yellow tick circles and one open row Water your plants with an empty circle.
takeaway: A plain count in the section header plus a tick circle on the right edge is the simplest done state, but strike through makes finished rows harder to read.

title: 0 / 3 complete with play or tick per row
what: A week strip, a large 0 / 3 complete heading, and cards tagged Self-care or Gratitude. Rows that open an activity show a play button, one shows 0 / 3 for a repeated task, and Drink a glass of water shows a tick button.
takeaway: The trailing control tells the user what a row does: play opens a session, a tick marks it in place, and a small count shows partial progress.

title: Today's plan with completed row collapsed
what: Today's plan with a first row reading All lessons finished, 3 lessons completed with a tick, then large icon rows Log your meals and Weigh in, and Start a Challenge with an Explore button.
takeaway: Finished items collapse into one summary row at the top so the next action is the most prominent thing on the screen.

title: Goals left for today with reward per row
what: A pet scene above 10 goals left for today!, then rows like Brush teeth, Take a stretch break and Do one thing that makes me happy, each with an icon, a 5 energy reward and a green tick button on the right.
takeaway: Counting what is left rather than what is done keeps the header pointing forward, and the reward on each row shows what one tick adds.

title: Today header pill 0 / 8 with anytime and planned groups
what: A small 0 / 8 pill top left, task rows like Start work 5m and Evening routine 10m with an emoji and an empty circle, Add a task for anytime, a PLANNED (0) group and 2h 8m Time left of day on a timeline.
takeaway: A tiny count pill in the header tracks the day without a big ring, and grouping into anytime and planned separates flexible tasks from timed ones.

title: Pausing an exercise
what: The running state with only the nose 4 and mouth 6 pill and nested circles reading Exhale; no controls are visible.
takeaway: Hide controls while breathing so the screen is only the shape and the phase word.

title: Pausing an exercise
what: After a tap the controls fade in: vibration, a pause button, settings and a 04:38 remaining pill, with the phase now Inhale.
takeaway: Tap anywhere to reveal pause and time left, so the controls are there when needed and gone when not.

title: Pausing an exercise
what: Paused at 04:31 with the circle frozen on Exhale, a square stop button and a large white play button side by side.
takeaway: Paused shows a big play and a smaller stop, the same resume first priority as Stoic.

title: Completing a task (breathing exercise)
what: Home with a SLEEP READINESS bar at 2/3 stars and a card MENTAL CLARITY, Center your breath, Balancing Breath, 1 min, Breathing Exercises and a Start button.
takeaway: A daily plan card with the minutes and a single Start sits under a progress bar for the day, the same shape as a Rhythm plan.

title: Completing a task (breathing exercise)
what: A dark screen with one sentence: Equal breaths steady your nervous system. This helps restore calm and presence.
takeaway: One line of why before the first breath, with no buttons, acts as a short settling moment.

title: Completing a task (breathing exercise)
what: A glowing orb with a thin ring and four phase dots, a bright marker moving round the ring, the words Breathe In and heart, pause and sound buttons, with an X top left.
takeaway: A marker travelling round a ring with one dot per phase shows where you are in the cycle without numbers.

title: Completing a task (breathing exercise)
what: The orb fades out, leaving only the ring with the marker at the bottom dot and the word Hold.
takeaway: Hold is shown by the shape going still and empty, a clear change from in and out.

title: Completing a task (breathing exercise)
what: The orb glows again with the marker back near the top and the words Breathe Out.
takeaway: Each phase gets one short word in the same spot, which is easy to follow for older eyes.

title: Completing a task (breathing exercise)
what: Back on Home the breathing card has shrunk to a dimmed row with a thumbnail and a grey tick, and the next card Move to center yourself is now first in full colour.
takeaway: The done item collapses and greys in place while the next one takes focus, a direct model for Up next.

title: Starting a guided breathing exercise
what: SESSION DETAILS for INCREASE RELAXATION with a short description, rows for BREATHING RATE BASIC 5s | 10s and DURATION 3 min, a video preview and a START EXERCISE button.
takeaway: Rate and duration as two labelled rows give the facts before starting, without a picker.

title: Starting a guided breathing exercise
what: The title INCREASE RELAXATION with 02:58 under it, an orange ring inside dotted guide circles, and the cue Inhale through the nose.
takeaway: A countdown under the title plus dotted guide circles that show the target size make the expansion easy to match.

title: Starting a guided breathing exercise
what: At 02:55 the orange ring has grown to the middle guide and the cue reads One more sharp inhale through the nose.
takeaway: Full sentence cues suit techniques like the physiological sigh where a single word would not be enough.

title: Starting a guided breathing exercise
what: At 02:53 the ring turns blue and fills the outer guide, with the cue Exhale slowly through the mouth and empty your lungs.
takeaway: Changing colour between inhale and exhale is a second signal for the phase beyond the word.

title: Starting a guided breathing exercise
what: A dark screen with a green circle tick and the single word SAVED.
takeaway: A brief saved confirmation tells the user the session counted before returning them.

title: Completing a breathing exercise
what: Courtyard Afternoon over a wind chime scene with page dots to swap scenes, a round breathing button in the middle, and Mute, Leave and Timer below.
takeaway: A start screen can be a calm scene with one round button, and the scene choice lives in swipeable dots.

title: Completing a breathing exercise
what: A large 3 with Stay relaxed and concentrate on your breath, and Leave at the bottom.
takeaway: A three second countdown with one calming line gives time to settle before the first breath.

title: Completing a breathing exercise
what: Breathe out above a short bar, a green mascot inside a soft white glow, and only Leave at the bottom.
takeaway: Only one control during the session keeps the focus on the shape.

title: Completing a breathing exercise
what: Breathe in with a filling bar and the hint Keep holding to leave above the Leave button.
takeaway: Press and hold to leave guards against accidental exits without an extra dialog, but needs a visible hint.

title: Completing a breathing exercise
what: Mindfulness Complete with the question Do you feel your mind is calmer? What's next?, a Start Focusing button and a Home link.
takeaway: The completion screen points straight at the next thing to do, which a daily plan can use to send people to the next item.
